candidate_fingerprint_fields: screen root XID, pixel geometry, root visual and depth
condition.proxy: existing research x11_delivery_proxy, transparent forwarding; no delay armed
record_separately: out-of-band Xvfb PID/start ticks and Unix socket inode for local servers
condition.server_b: independent Xvfb :90 with identical launch arguments

decision_rule: Do not use an advertised setup fingerprint as an admission-fence key unless it is alias-stable and distinguishes the independent X server. This experiment does not authorize an implementation or establish a Windows desktop identity.
primary_discriminator: Candidate fingerprint matches for all three paths to server A and differs for independent server B. A collision across A/B means advertised setup fields are not a unique surface identity; a mismatch between A aliases means the fingerprint is not alias-stable.
purpose: Determine whether X11 server setup metadata can stably identify one shared input surface across direct Unix, direct TCP, and a TCP proxy display alias, while distinguishing a second Xvfb server.
scope: Synthetic Xvfb protocol metadata only; not WSLg, Windows, native GUI, MAP01, or production admission.
stop_rule: One read-only probe run; no retries or task inputs.
